saw_lines: Teachers buy lesson tools to get their weekends back, then judge each tool by the first lesson it produces.
So the sale is won or lost in the first line, when a teacher decides if the lesson is worth it.
Your 10 copy ads carry 0 proof numbers, so new teachers have nothing concrete to trust. Open every new ad with a real figure, such as your review count.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 17 Nov 2026
points: 0 of 10 copy ads carry a proof number, so a teacher seeing Chalkie cold has nothing concrete to trust before clicking. Pick a figure you can stand behind, such as your review count, and open every new ad with it.
0 of 10 copy ads mention an offer, so a new teacher has no reason to start today. Build new ads around a first month offer on Chalkie Max, named in the opening line, so the click has a reason.

Your 10 copy ads open with 7 different stories, and the most used opener runs on 2 ads, so a teacher who sees one gets the same hook again. Keep the 2 strongest openings and build the next batch from them.

2 ads have run 60+ days, which is evidence the activity sheets opener works, yet most of your copy does not reuse it. Build new versions with a different subject or year group, and run them against the original.

ads_1: Activity sheet openers with a real figure, tested against the Sunday planning hook.
